characters: Eyram Hormeku: a 14-year-old girl in a school uniform, with a notebook, standing with a basket of vegetables.
Mr Dadzie: the agriculture teacher, in a plain shirt, with a map of India and a drawing of milk cans.
Yaw Agyemang: a 13-year-old boy in a school uniform, with his hand raised.
The village buyer: a man in a cap with a notebook, standing beside a pickup truck full of crates.

narrationPlan.voice: A strong, fair-minded girl’s voice for Eyram; a warm storyteller’s voice for Mr Dadzie
narrationPlan.pace: Clear and story-like, slowing for the grammar rules on the last pages (about 118 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Warm, steady drums with a gentle flute; a lifting chorus at the mock meeting (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Eyram, Mr Dadzie, Yaw and the village buyer are invented. The buyer is not presented as a villain; he is shown as one person in a village that has no choice of buyers. The Anand facts come from an encyclopaedia account of Amul: founded in 1946 as the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers’ Union; a private company had an effective monopoly on collecting milk from Kaira and supplying it to Mumbai; prices were set arbitrarily; a three-tier structure of village societies, district unions and a state federation; 3.6 million milk producers; the account says that under its long-time leader the primary producer received the largest share of the consumer’s rupee, without a percentage.

The story says that Amul took decades to grow and that cooperatives can fail through poor records, dishonest leaders and weak sales. It does not claim that the Anand pattern can be copied in Ghana. It does not state how cooperatives are registered in Ghana; it tells readers to ask.
The reported-speech examples follow standard rules: backshift of tenses, changed pronouns and time words, and “whether” for a yes-or-no question.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?

Check the Anand facts (the 1946 date, the three-tier structure, the 3.6 million producers) against a more authoritative source such as Amul’s own account or a dairy-development source, and update or label the figures as dated.
Check how farmer cooperatives are registered and supervised in Ghana (for example with the department responsible for cooperatives) and add the current office to the guide.
Check the reported-speech examples and rules against the NaCCA English syllabus.

teacherGuide.overview: A story about how small farmers can own the link that pays them, told through the Anand dairy cooperative in India. It shows the risks of cooperatives as well as the benefits and models reported speech.
learningGoals: Describe the three levels of the Anand cooperative.
Give two reasons a cooperative can fail.
Change direct speech to reported speech with correct tense, pronouns and time words.
beforeReading: Ask: who decides the price of what your family sells or buys? What happens if there is only one buyer?
whileReading: At page 3, ask learners to draw the three boxes before looking at the page.
afterReading: Hold a mock cooperative meeting with a chair, secretary and treasurer, and write three rules.
Write six sentences in direct speech and change them to reported speech.
discussion: Why might a farmers’ group have more power than one farmer?
What could members do to keep leaders honest?
reflection: What would you want from a group before you trusted it with your money or your crop?

mathsExtension.task: Suppose a cooperative has 4 villages with 25 members each. How many members are there?
If each member pays a joining fee of GH¢10 (an imaginary figure), how much do they collect?

support: Give a reported-speech chart with direct, reported, and the changes: tense, pronoun, time word.
stretch: Write a formal letter to a district office asking how a farmers’ group can be registered as a cooperative, with the eight formal-letter features.

localiseThis: Ask your district agriculture office or the department responsible for cooperatives how a group is registered and what support exists; use local crops and groups instead of the Indian example.

factCheck.claim: Amul began in 1946 when small dairy farmers in the Kaira district formed a cooperative so that they could sell milk directly instead of through a company with an effective monopoly on collecting milk and supplying Mumbai; it has a three-tier structure of village societies, district unions and a state federation; it is reported to have 3.6 million milk producers.
factCheck.explanation: From an encyclopaedia account; the producer figure is its present-tense report and the account gives no percentage for the farmer’s share.
factCheck.reference: Wikipedia, “Amul” (en.wikipedia.org). Verify with Amul or a dairy-development source.
